subject: Next steps — surge window readiness & activation SLAs
messages:
From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Zhang <alex.zhang@clearbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: surge window & activation SLAs (recap + proposed acceptance criteria)

Alex — thanks for a productive 45m today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on what Redwood needs to validate to meet ClearBank's peak-period requirements. I attached a first-pass runbook and the capacity snapshot you shared.

High-level ask from ClearBank: sustain baseline throughput during business hours, and absorb a 10x burst during payment-clearing surges while preserving P95 latency targets for the critical streaming endpoints.

Proposed acceptance criteria (please confirm):
- Latency: P95 text generation <= 350ms for non-streaming API; streaming first-token <= 120ms and steady-state token delta P95 <= 40ms.
- Concurrency/throughput: baseline sustained concurrency = 300 sessions (avg request size 1.2k tokens), burst peak concurrency = 2,400 sessions for up to 6 minutes.
- Scale-up time: 90% of burst requests should be served without queueing when warm pool is primed; otherwise queueing time must be < 10s. Target time-to-scale (cold) <= 75s, warm-pool activation within 10s.
- Fallback behavior: automatic fallback to a smaller compatible model within 600ms if latency degrades beyond thresholds; explicit circuit-breaker to avoid systemic failure.

Operational notes / assumptions:
- We will use prefix/KV caching and pre-seeded warm pool to reduce cold-starts during the surge window.
- Warm pool sizing suggestion in attached runbook: prewarm 150 instances (config depends on model variant).
- Telemetry we will collect: per-token latency, queue-depth, warm-pool hit ratio, model-fallback counts, and tail-error rates.

Requested next steps (owners + dates):
1) ClearBank: confirm the P95 latency targets and exposure to streaming-first-token requirement (Alex/ops) — request by Fri 2026-06-11 EOD.
2) Redwood Eng (Karthik): confirm feasibility of warm pool sizing + test plan for a synthetic 10x burst — target 2026-06-15.
3) Redwood Sales/SE (Marissa): schedule a 60-min follow-up ops runbook review with ClearBank ops — propose Mon 2026-06-14.
4) Both teams: sign off on a 2-hour live test window (staging) and a success checklist.

Attachments referenced: surge_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook stub), clearbank_capacity_snapshot.csv (customer traffic snapshot).

If anything above reads wrong or you want the numbers tightened, flag it and we'll update the runbook.

—Ethan
Ethan Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ethan_park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alex Zhang <alex.zhang@clearbank.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
Cc: ClearBank Ops <ops@clearbank.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: surge window & activation SLAs (recap + proposed acceptance criteria)

Ethan / team — thanks for the write-up, that aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Latency: the streaming-first-token SLA is critical for the UX on mobile checkout (we should treat that as a hard requirement). 120ms is aggressive but acceptable if measured end-to-end. If it's not achievable we need clear fallback behavior (show loading indicator, degrade gracefully).

2) Burst shape: our traffic spikes are asymmetric — 60% of burst volume arrives within the first 90s, the rest tapers over the next 4–5 minutes. Hitting the first 90s is most important.

3) Warm pool: ops prefers warm pool activation within 5–10s for the first tranche; ops will need to understand cost/commit tradeoffs.

4) Test window: we can make a staging window available on Tue 2026-06-22 22:00–00:00 UTC (this maps to our peak for the subset of customers that will be in scope). Can Redwood run a seeded synthetic workload for the 2-hour window?

Items for Redwood to confirm:
- A concrete warm-pool size recommendation and expected wasted capacity at baseline (ops needs cost estimate).
- The exact metrics Redwood will publish during the test and the dashboard link.

We can share a short Ops runbook on our side (ops team will upload a traffic replay snippet).

Thanks — Alex
Alex Zhang
Director, Payments Platform — ClearBank
alex.zhang@clearbank.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Zhang <alex.zhang@clearbank.com>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: surge window & activation SLAs (recap + proposed acceptance criteria)

Alex — great notes. I'll own scheduling and the runbook review session. Quick pragmatic updates from infra/SE: 

- Warm-pool recommendation: start with prewarming 180 instances for the preferred model variant (gptx-std-8q). We estimate ~22% unused capacity at baseline for that configuration (cost estimate attached).
- Test plan outline (we'll deliver a detailed doc by Mon 2026-06-14):
  * Pre-seed KV cache with representative prefixes.
  * Execute a 3-stage storm: 1) ramp to 2.5K concurrent over 90s, 2) hold peak for 4 minutes, 3) taper.
  * Monitor: P95 latency (non-stream), first-token stream latency, queue depth, warm-pool hit rate, fallback events.
  * Success criteria: P95 and first-token targets met for >= 90% of traffic during the first 90s; no more than 1% request fallback to smaller model.
- Dashboards/telemetry: we'll publish a temporary dashboard (Grafana link will be created) and stream per-token latency and queue metrics to the shared drive.
- Run ownership: Karthik (Infra) to run the priming and scale validation; I'll coordinate scheduling with ClearBank ops and document rollback steps.

Action items (owners):
- Marissa: send calendar invite for ops runbook review, include runbook + test plan draft by Mon 2026-06-14.
- Karthik: confirm warm-pool script and target instance count; test dry-run by 2026-06-18.
- Ethan: confirm engagement and get ClearBank sign-off on P95 numbers by Fri EOD.

Attachments: updated_surge_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook notes + cost estimate).

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: surge window & activation SLAs (recap + proposed acceptance criteria)

Ack — I'll own the priming test and run the dry-run on 2026-06-18 as discussed. Quick notes for the team: 
- I'll instrument a short pre-seed job to warm KV caches and validate warm-pool hit rates before the staged storm.
- I'll publish a short checklist (pre-run, during-run, post-run) and attach the script to the runbook.
- Marissa: please loop me into the calendar invite for Tue 6/22 staging window with ClearBank ops — want a 30-minute sync 24h before the live run.
